correctness.rationale: For every k>=2, exact half-open branch substitution yields the 2k-point reflected induced-core graph, stationary weights by detailed balance and a positive-gate irreducible chain. Independently, for every 0<delta<=1/6, physical f0/f1 send the two-sided dyadic lattice q_j to q_{j-1}/q_{j+1} respectively. Fair independent map choices therefore yield a genuine simple symmetric random walk on Z. Levy's classical arcsine law gives the claimed original-time occupation limit; fixed starting shifts and visits to the origin are negligible by O(sqrt N) expected local-time bounds. The cosine vectors prove the finite spectrum. Exact-rational checker passed all 22,648 core nodes and 705 physical nodes; finite tests are not substituted for universal algebra and classic limit theorem.

originality.rationale: The main original mathematical component is an explicit infinite family of qualifying irreducible finite core measures for the formerly untreated parameter interval delta<1/8, partly answering Nakamura et al. Problem 1.8. Its known core theorem establishes a conditional limit law, not the explicit stationary core graph. The secondary direct pointwise arcsine result uses an independent simple random walk identity and classic Levy theorem; it is not represented as a new general arcsine principle and only applies to countable dyadic starting positions. Primary-source and published-finding corpus searches found no decisive stronger source or exact table, though simple symbolic observations could be implicit in other literature.
residual_risks: A specialized paper or note may have independently described the dyadic small-parameter invariant core despite no match in inspected research records.
The theorem establishes a finite supported arcine law at each parameter; it does not resolve almost-everywhere initial condition statements or the original all-delta question.
Related published record full texts were not inspected because the indexed summaries describe different mathematical objects; priority could be revisited with broader literature access.

The direct dyadic-index simple random walk is an elementary identity and might be implicit in standard presentations; the constructive infinite family of small-delta finite core invariant measures is the principal scientific-value contribution.

value.rationale: The explicit infinite dyadic sequence delta=2^{-(k+2)}<1/8 yields qualifying invariant measures for a previously unresolved core-existence subfamily of the source problem, with meaningful linear core-size and inverse-quadratic spectral-gap scaling as the perturbation tends to zero. A distinct exact conjugacy identifies every physical dyadic orbit for all permitted positive delta with a simple symmetric walk, yielding a pointwise Levy arcsine limit at a countable set; that elementary corollary is not the sole asserted contribution. The work does not generalize core existence to every delta or initial state.
